newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's FFK halts Gazprom electronic trade.
newsitem.headline: Russia's FFK halts Gazprom electronic trade.

text.p: Russia's Federal Securities Corporation (FFK) said on Wednesday it had stopped electronic trade in domestic Gazprom shares.

"We took the decision to stop trade (in Gazprom) from today on the electronic system," FFK President Alexander Voloshin told a round table of journalists and traders, adding weekly auctions and specialised trading sessions in Gazprom would continue.

The FFK is a relatively small market for domestic Gazprom shares in comparison to the larger Russian Trading System (RTS) but had the advantage of not having to offer Gazprom the right of first refusal in all trades, a requirement RTS traders face.
The RTS is an over-the-counter type market on which trade is less transparent than at exchanges.
Voloshin said the FFK had failed to reach agreement to transfer its Gazprom trading to the Moscow Stock Exchange before trading began on that exchange this month.

The Moscow Stock Exchange was one of four regional exchanges named in a government order at the end of May and given permission to trade Gazprom shares without offering Gazprom a right of first refusal from July 1.

The government and Gazprom are trying to increase share transparency and so are trying to limit unconditional trade of domestic shares of Gazprom, one of Russia's largest companies, to so-called organised markets.
Foreigners may not buy domestic Gazprom shares and are required to purchase American Depositary Shares, which cover domestic shares but are traded abroad.
The FFK does not have a licence from the Federal Commission on the Securities Market, the markets watchdog, which would have prolonged its right to trade Gazprom without offering first refusal.

Formerly it organised auctions and electronic trading sessions of Gazprom shares in which Gazprom's right of refusal was waived by agreement. It is also the main agent for auctions of government property.

Gazprom shares on the Moscow exchange eased to 3,434 on Wednesday on volume of 1.60 billion roubles ($276,577) from 3,470 roubles on July 1, the first day of trade. Turnover was 665.5 million roubles ($115,056) on July 1.
The government order issued in May has confused market participants, who say the status of many trading systems, including the RTS, is not clear.

"The document is far from perfect," said Voloshin. "It gives rise to a mass of questions that have yet to be answered...The faster we get the explanations, the more clarity there will be on the market and the less damage there will be to the market." ($=5,785 roubles)
